transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you to the clinic?
I just don’t feel like doing any of the things I used to love anymore, even painting or going to my dance class. I just... I don't really know what's happened to me lately.
How long have you been feeling this way—has it been at least two weeks, or has it been going on for a year or more?

It’s been going on for about four months now. It really started to take hold after my youngest daughter moved away and they cut back the arts programs at the community center. Since then, I've just felt so empty and lost.
Have you felt down or depressed most days during these four months, or has this kind of low mood been going on for at least two years?

Yes, I've felt very down and empty almost every day for these past four months, and I often find myself just sitting and crying. It definitely hasn't been going on for two years, only since everything changed after my daughter left.
Have you had any thoughts that life is not worth living, or thoughts of hurting yourself?
Yes, I often think it would be much easier for everyone if I just didn't wake up in the morning. I've even pictured taking all of my blood pressure pills at once, though I haven't actually done it.
Have you also noticed changes in your sleep, appetite, or energy level during these past four months?

My energy is just completely gone, and even simple things like getting dressed or making breakfast wear me out so much that I have to sit right back down. I'm not really sure about my sleep or appetite, but this heavy exhaustion has just taken over everything these past four months.
Did these symptoms begin after a specific stressful event, and have they been mostly tied to that stressor, or do they feel present even when you are not thinking about it?

Yes, it definitely started right after my daughter moved away and the community center cut the arts programs. But now, this heavy, empty feeling is just there all the time, even when I'm not actively thinking about those changes.

Besides the changes with your daughter and the community center, have you had any other major stressors or losses around the time this started? Or do the symptoms feel out of proportion to that stress and present most of the day, nearly every day?

No, there weren't any other big changes or losses, just those two things. But the sadness I feel now is just so overwhelming and out of proportion, and this heavy, empty feeling is there almost every single day, most of the day.
Do these symptoms ever fully go away when you are not thinking about the stressors, or have they been present most of the day nearly every day for the past four months?

No, they never fully go away. This heavy, empty feeling has been there nearly every single day for the past four months, and trying to distract myself doesn't make it disappear. It's just constant, no matter what I do.
Have you had any thoughts of killing yourself, or made any plans to act on those thoughts?

Like I said, I do sometimes think it would be easier for everyone if I just didn't wake up. I have pictured taking all my blood pressure pills at once, but I haven't actually made a real plan to do it. I would never want to hurt my family like that, even if I feel like a burden.
Do you feel sad or lose interest in things even when you are not thinking about the life changes that started this, or do the feelings come and go mainly in response to those stressors?

No, they don't come and go—this sadness and loss of interest are constant. Most days I wake up with a heavy, empty feeling in my chest and cry over nothing in particular, even when I'm not thinking about my daughter or the center. I just feel completely blank and have no desire to paint or dance anymore, no matter what.

Did these symptoms start within about 3 months of the stressor, and have they been mainly a reaction to that event, or do they feel like a depressive episode that came on independently and lasted most of the day nearly every day?

Yes, they started about two months after my daughter moved and the center cut its programs. But it feels like a deep, constant depression rather than just a simple reaction, and I wake up every single day with this heavy, empty feeling in my chest.
Have you also had other depression symptoms such as changes in sleep or appetite, trouble concentrating, feeling slowed down or agitated, or feelings of worthlessness or excessive guilt?

Yes, I feel extremely slowed down; my husband even teases me that I move like I'm "underwater" because I shuffle around so slowly. I also carry this constant guilt, feeling like a useless burden and believing that everyone drifting away is somehow my fault. My sleep, appetite, or concentration haven't really been the main issues, though.
Did the symptoms begin within 3 months of the stressful event, and have they mainly been a direct reaction to that event rather than a depressive episode that seems to have started on its own?

Yes, they started about four months ago, which was about two months after my daughter moved and the center cut its programs. While it felt like a direct reaction to those losses at first, it has now spiraled into a deep, heavy, and constant sadness. It just feels much bigger and harder to shake than a normal reaction to life changing.
Did the stressful events involve anything traumatic or life-threatening, and since then have you had nightmares, flashbacks, or felt constantly on edge or avoid reminders of it?

No, it wasn't anything traumatic or life-threatening like that. It was just my daughter moving away and the community center cutting its programs, and I don't have any nightmares, flashbacks, or feel constantly on edge.
Have you been having any nightmares, flashbacks, feeling on edge, or avoiding reminders of the events since this started?

No, I don't have any nightmares, flashbacks, or feel on edge in that way. My struggles are really more about the heavy sadness, emptiness, and feeling like a constant burden. I don't experience any trauma-related reminders or anything like that.
Did your symptoms begin within 3 months of the stressful event and seem mainly tied to that event, or did they start independently and persist most days regardless of reminders of it?

Yes, they really took hold about four months ago, which was a couple of months after my daughter moved and the center cut its programs. But now, this heavy, empty feeling is there almost every single day when I wake up, regardless of whether I am actively thinking about those changes.
Before these changes with your daughter and the community center, had you ever had a similar period of depression or loss of interest lasting at least two weeks?

No, I have never experienced anything like this before in my life. For years, my life was very active, full of joy, and centered around my family and the community center. This heavy sadness and loss of interest only started about four months ago after those major changes.

Before this episode started, had you ever had any similar periods of depression or loss of interest lasting at least two weeks? Also, do you feel the sadness is mainly a reaction to the recent changes, or does it seem to have started on its own and persist most days regardless of them?

I don't think I have ever experienced a period of depression or loss of interest like this before. While the sadness seemed to start after my daughter moved and the community center cut its programs, it now just feels like a heavy, constant presence most days regardless of what is happening, and I'm not entirely sure how to separate them.
Did your symptoms start within 3 months of the stressful event and seem mainly tied to that event, or did they begin on their own and continue most days even when you are not thinking about it?

Yes, they started about four months ago, which was a couple of months after my daughter moved and the center cut its programs. Now, this heavy and empty feeling is there most days and feels completely constant, continuing even when I'm not actively thinking about those events.

Do you feel your low mood and loss of interest are mainly a reaction to the life changes, or do they seem to have started on their own and persist most days even when you are not thinking about those changes?

They definitely started after those big life changes with my daughter and the center. But now, this heavy, empty feeling and loss of interest are there almost every single day, persisting even when I'm not thinking about those things at all. It just feels like it has taken on a life of its own now.

Did the sadness and loss of interest begin within about 3 months of the life changes, and do they feel mainly like a reaction to those stressors rather than a depressive episode that started on its own?

Yes, they started within a couple of months of those changes, so it was definitely within that time. It really feels like a reaction to those painful losses, because I was doing completely fine and was so active before they happened. But now, it's just grown into this heavy, constant weight.

Before these life changes happened, did you ever have any periods of depression or loss of interest lasting at least two weeks? Also, since the changes, do your symptoms feel mainly tied to the stressor, or do they continue even when you are not thinking about it?

No, before these changes I never experienced any depression or lost interest in things; my life was always very busy, active, and filled with my family and community events. Now, though, this heavy, empty feeling and lack of interest are constant throughout the day. I find myself crying over nothing in particular, even when I'm not actively thinking about the changes at all.
Besides feeling sad and losing interest, have you had other symptoms like changes in sleep, appetite, concentration, or feeling slowed down nearly every day for at least two weeks?

Yes, I have been feeling very slowed down every day for the last four months; my husband even says I move like I'm underwater because it takes me so long to get up or answer questions. I also feel constantly exhausted, but I'm not really sure about changes in my sleep, appetite, or concentration.

Over the past four months, have you had several other depression symptoms nearly every day, such as major changes in sleep or appetite, trouble concentrating, feeling worthless or excessively guilty, or feeling slowed down or agitated?

Yes, over the last four months I have definitely experienced several of those. I constantly feel like a useless burden to my family and blame myself for everyone drifting away. I also feel incredibly slowed down, and my husband even teases me that I move like I'm underwater because I shuffle so slowly.
Did your low mood and loss of interest start only after the stressful changes, or had you ever had a period of depression that began on its own without a clear trigger?
Yes, this low mood and loss of interest only started after those stressful changes about four months ago. Before that, I had never experienced a period of depression like this in my entire life.
Have you had any thoughts of killing yourself, and if so, have you made any specific plan or taken any steps toward doing it?

Yes, I do have thoughts that it would be much easier for everyone if I just didn't wake up one morning. I've even found myself picturing taking all my blood pressure pills at once, but I haven't actually taken any steps or made a real plan to do it.
Did your symptoms start mainly as a reaction to the stressful life changes, or did they begin on their own and keep going even when you were not thinking about those changes?

They definitely started right after my daughter moved away and the community center cut its programs, because losing those roles made me feel so empty. But now, these heavy feelings, the constant tiredness, and even hearing my daughter's voice saying cruel things have taken over completely. It stays with me all the time, even when I'm not actively thinking about those events.
Have you been hearing or seeing things that other people do not, or feeling very suspicious or confused about what is real?

Yes, it's a bit embarrassing to admit, but I have been hearing things and feeling very suspicious lately. Sometimes I clearly hear my daughter's voice in the hallway saying that I just drag everyone down, even though she lives hours away and the house is completely quiet. I've also become deeply convinced that my family is planning to abandon me because I'm such a burden, and it really frightens me.
Have you been hearing or seeing things that other people do not, or feeling unusually suspicious that others are trying to harm or abandon you?

Yes, it's so frightening, but I clearly hear my daughter's voice in the hallway saying I just drag everyone down and they'd be better off without me, even when the house is quiet. I've also become deeply convinced that my family is planning to abandon me because I'm such a burden. These scary voices and thoughts only started happening after this heavy sadness took over a few months ago.
Have you been hearing or seeing things that other people do not, or feeling unusually suspicious that others are trying to harm or abandon you?

Yes, I've been hearing my daughter's voice in the hallway saying hurtful things like I just drag everyone down, even though she lives hours away and the house is quiet. I also feel deeply convinced and terrified that my family is planning to abandon me because I've become such a useless burden. These scary voices and thoughts only started after this heavy sadness took over.
